reason: The agent correctly navigated to the monthly report and read the counts, but formatted the final response as numeric month codes (`01:12, 02:7, ...`) rather than the reference’s month-name-and-unit phrasing. It needed to answer `January: 12 orders, Feburary: 7 orders, March: 5 orders, April: 9 orders, May: 5 orders` to satisfy the grader.

The agent correctly retrieved the five counts, but returned them in compact numeric form (`01:12, 02:7, ...`). The grader expected month-name entries with the unit, e.g. `January: 12 orders`, `Feburary: 7 orders`, through `May: 5 orders`. It needed to present the retrieved values in that expected wording/structure.

It needed to reproduce the expected month labels and include the word `orders` for each count.

The agent correctly navigated to the monthly Complete-order report and extracted all counts, but its final numeric shorthand (`02:16, 03:14, ...`) did not match the grader’s expected month-name phrasing with the `orders` suffix. It needed to return entries such as `Feburary: 16 orders`, `March: 14 orders`, through `November: 5 orders` (including the reference’s spellings).

The agent incorrectly equated Magento’s “Any” status (all statuses except canceled) with “successful orders.” This included one non-successful April order, producing 04:8 instead of the reference 04:7. It needed to filter for the appropriate successful order status(es), or inspect statuses to exclude the extra April order; the other monthly counts matched.

The agent correctly navigated to the Complete-orders monthly report and read all ten counts, but its final response used numeric labels such as `02:16` and omitted the month names and `orders` wording expected by the grader’s fuzzy-match reference. It needed to present entries like `February: 16 orders`, `March: 14 orders`, through `November: 5 orders` (matching the reference phrasing).

The agent correctly retrieved all monthly counts, but the final response used numeric `MM:COUNT` entries (`02:16`, etc.) rather than the grader’s expected month-name phrases with the `orders` suffix (e.g., `Feburary: 16 orders`, `March: 14 orders`, …). It needed to present the values in the reference answer’s accepted textual format.

The agent correctly navigated to the completed-orders monthly report and read all ten counts, but formatted the response as numeric month codes (e.g. `02:16`) rather than the reference-compatible month-name entries with the word `orders` (e.g. `Feburary: 16 orders`). It needed to present each count using the expected month labels and wording.

The agent incorrectly treated Magento’s “Any” status (all non-canceled orders) as equivalent to successful orders. This included one unsuccessful/refunded or closed April order, producing 04:8 instead of the reference 04:7. It needed to use the appropriate specified successful statuses or otherwise exclude that order; the other monthly counts were correct.
